nodes.description: Shortened refractoriness and/or impaired coupling create an atrial substrate that supports multiple coexisting reentrant wavelets and ectopic triggers, initiating and maintaining atrial fibrillation. As AF persists, electrical remodeling further shortens refractoriness ("AF begets AF").

evidence.reference_title: KCNQ1 gain-of-function mutation in familial atrial fibrillation.
evidence.snippet: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is a common cardiac arrhythmia whose molecular etiology is poorly understood.

nodes.description: In GJA5-related familial AF, variants in connexin 40 impair gap-junction assembly and intercellular electrical coupling between atrial myocytes, producing heterogeneous, slowed atrial conduction that promotes reentry. This is a coupling/conduction mechanism that converges on the same arrhythmogenic substrate as the channelopathy arm.

evidence.reference_title: Somatic mutations in the connexin 40 gene (GJA5) in atrial fibrillation.
evidence.snippet: The cardiac gap-junction protein connexin 40 is expressed selectively in atrial myocytes and mediates the coordinated electrical activation of the atria.

evidence.reference_title: Somatic mutations in the connexin 40 gene (GJA5) in atrial fibrillation.
evidence.snippet: Mutations in GJA5 may predispose patients to idiopathic atrial fibrillation by impairing gap-junction assembly or electrical coupling.

nodes.description: A germline (or, for GJA5, atrial-tissue-restricted somatic) variant alters an atrial ion channel, a gap-junction protein, or another atrial-restricted protein. The best-characterized variants are gain-of-function in atrial potassium channels (KCNQ1/IKs, KCNJ2/IK1, KCNE2), with additional families carrying GJA5 (connexin 40), NPPA, SCN5A, and loss-of-function KCNA5 (IKur) variants. Three further loci reach this node without a pore-forming potassium or sodium channel being the mutated protein: ABCC9 encodes SUR2A, the regulatory rather than pore-forming subunit of the KATP channel; NUP155 is a nuclear pore component; and MYL4 encodes the atrial-selective essential myosin light chain. The sodium channel beta subunits SCN1B and SCN2B act indirectly, by reducing SCN5A-mediated current.

evidence.reference_title: KCNQ1 gain-of-function mutation in familial atrial fibrillation.
evidence.snippet: We studied a family with hereditary persistent AF and identified the causative mutation (S140G) in the KCNQ1 (KvLQT1) gene on chromosome 11p15.5.

evidence.reference_title: A Kir2.1 gain-of-function mutation underlies familial atrial fibrillation.
evidence.snippet: A valine-to-isoleucine mutation at position 93 (V93I) of Kir2.1 was found in all affected members in one kindred.

evidence.reference_title: Somatic mutations in the connexin 40 gene (GJA5) in atrial fibrillation.
evidence.snippet: Four novel heterozygous missense mutations were identified in 4 of the 15 patients.

evidence.reference_title: Kv1.5 channelopathy due to KCNA5 loss-of-function mutation causes human atrial fibrillation.
evidence.snippet: The heterozygous E375X mutation, present in a familial case of atrial fibrillation and absent in 540 unrelated control individuals, introduced a premature stop codon disrupting the Kv1.5 channel protein.

evidence.reference_title: Kv1.5 channelopathy due to KCNA5 loss-of-function mutation causes human atrial fibrillation.
evidence.snippet: Genomic DNA scanning revealed a nonsense mutation in KCNA5 that encodes Kv1.5, a voltage-gated potassium channel expressed in human atria.

evidence.reference_title: Kv1.5 channelopathy due to KCNA5 loss-of-function mutation causes human atrial fibrillation.
evidence.snippet: Loss of channel function translated into action potential prolongation and early after-depolarization in human atrial myocytes, increasing vulnerability to stress-provoked triggered activity.

evidence.reference_title: Identification of a KCNE2 gain-of-function mutation in patients with familial atrial fibrillation.
evidence.snippet: The mutation was present in all affected members in the two kindreds and was absent in 462 healthy unrelated Chinese subjects.

evidence.reference_title: Identification of a KCNE2 gain-of-function mutation in patients with familial atrial fibrillation.
evidence.snippet: An arginine-to-cysteine mutation at position 27 (R27C) of KCNE2, the beta subunit of the KCNQ1-KCNE2 channel responsible for a background potassium current, was found in 2 of the 28 probands.

evidence.reference_title: Identification of a KCNE2 gain-of-function mutation in patients with familial atrial fibrillation.
evidence.snippet: Similar to KCNQ1 S140G, the mutation had a gain-of-function effect on the KCNQ1-KCNE2 channel; unlike long QT syndrome-associated KCNE2 mutations, it did not alter HERG-KCNE2 current.

evidence.reference_title: A Kir2.1 gain-of-function mutation underlies familial atrial fibrillation.
evidence.snippet: Kir2.1 V93I mutation may play a role in initiating and/or maintaining AF by increasing the activity of the inward rectifier K(+) channel.

evidence.reference_title: KCNQ1 gain-of-function mutation in familial atrial fibrillation.
evidence.snippet: Functional analysis of the S140G mutant revealed a gain-of-function effect on the KCNQ1/KCNE1 and the KCNQ1/KCNE2 currents, which contrasts with the dominant negative or loss-of-function effects of the KCNQ1 mutations previously identified in patients with long QT syndrome.

evidence.reference_title: A frameshift deletion in the sarcomere gene MYL4 causes early-onset familial atrial fibrillation.
evidence.snippet: We found eight homozygous carriers of the mutation, all of whom had early-onset AF.

evidence.reference_title: A frameshift deletion in the sarcomere gene MYL4 causes early-onset familial atrial fibrillation.
evidence.snippet: We discovered a rare frameshift deletion in the myosin MYL4 gene (c.234delC) that associates with early-onset AF under a recessive mode of inheritance (allelic frequency = 0.58%).

evidence.reference_title: A frameshift deletion in the sarcomere gene MYL4 causes early-onset familial atrial fibrillation.
evidence.snippet: Through a population approach we found a loss of function mutation in the myosin gene MYL4 that, in the homozygous state, is completely penetrant for early-onset AF.

evidence.reference_title: A frameshift deletion in the sarcomere gene MYL4 causes early-onset familial atrial fibrillation.
evidence.snippet: Three of the homozygotes had received pacemaker implantations due to sick sinus syndrome, three had suffered an ischemic stroke, and one suffered sudden cardiac death.

evidence.reference_title: Dysfunction of Myosin Light-Chain 4 (MYL4) Leads to Heritable Atrial Cardiomyopathy With Electrical, Contractile, and Structural Components: Evidence From Genetically-Engineered Rats.
evidence.snippet: Myosin light-chain 4 (MYL4), encoding the atrial-selective essential myosin light chain, was identified as a candidate gene.

evidence.reference_title: Dysfunction of Myosin Light-Chain 4 (MYL4) Leads to Heritable Atrial Cardiomyopathy With Electrical, Contractile, and Structural Components: Evidence From Genetically-Engineered Rats.
evidence.snippet: The mutation cosegregated with atrial standstill (selected as the principal presenting trait) with a logarithm of the odds score of 5.3.

evidence.reference_title: Dysfunction of Myosin Light-Chain 4 (MYL4) Leads to Heritable Atrial Cardiomyopathy With Electrical, Contractile, and Structural Components: Evidence From Genetically-Engineered Rats.
evidence.snippet: Both MYL4 p.E11K knock-in rats and MYL4 knockout rats showed progressive atrial electrophysiological, contractile, and fibrotic abnormalities, similar to affected patients.

evidence.reference_title: Atrial natriuretic peptide frameshift mutation in familial atrial fibrillation.
evidence.snippet: In a family with 11 clinically affected members, we mapped an atrial fibrillation locus to chromosome 1p36-p35 and identified a heterozygous frameshift mutation in the gene encoding atrial natriuretic peptide.

evidence.reference_title: Atrial natriuretic peptide frameshift mutation in familial atrial fibrillation.
evidence.snippet: Circulating chimeric atrial natriuretic peptide (ANP) was detected in high concentration in subjects with the mutation, and shortened atrial action potentials were seen in an isolated heart model, creating a possible substrate for atrial fibrillation.

evidence.reference_title: Mutation in nuclear pore component NUP155 leads to atrial fibrillation and early sudden cardiac death.
evidence.snippet: We have identified a homozygous mutation, R391H, in NUP155 that cosegregates with AF, affects nuclear localization of NUP155, and reduces nuclear envelope permeability.

evidence.reference_title: Mutation in nuclear pore component NUP155 leads to atrial fibrillation and early sudden cardiac death.
evidence.snippet: Homozygous NUP155(-/-) knockout mice die before E8.5, but heterozygous NUP155(+/-) mice show the AF phenotype.

evidence.reference_title: Mutation in nuclear pore component NUP155 leads to atrial fibrillation and early sudden cardiac death.
evidence.snippet: The R391H mutation and reduction of NUP155 are associated with inhibition of both export of Hsp70 mRNA and nuclear import of Hsp70 protein.

evidence.reference_title: Cardiac sodium channel (SCN5A) variants associated with atrial fibrillation.
evidence.snippet: In 10 probands (2.7%), 8 novel variants not found in the control population (0%; P=0.001) were identified.

evidence.reference_title: Cardiac sodium channel (SCN5A) variants associated with atrial fibrillation.
evidence.snippet: Mutations or rare variants in SCN5A may predispose patients with or without underlying heart disease to AF.

evidence.reference_title: Cardiac sodium channel (SCN5A) variants associated with atrial fibrillation.
evidence.snippet: We also identified 11 rare missense variants in 12 probands (3.2%) that have previously been associated with inherited arrhythmia syndromes (eg, congenital long-QT syndrome and Brugada syndrome).

nodes.description: Enhanced atrial repolarizing current shortens the atrial action potential duration and effective refractory period. A shorter refractory period reduces the wavelength of atrial reentry, allowing more simultaneous reentrant wavelets to be accommodated within the atria. KCNQ1, KCNE2 and KCNJ2 reach this node by gain of function; KCNA5 does not, and is modelled on the opposite route - loss of IKur lengthens rather than shortens the atrial action potential and produces early afterdepolarizations instead.

nodes.description: The clinical manifestation: paroxysmal, persistent, or permanent atrial fibrillation, typically with earlier onset than acquired AF and often in structurally normal hearts. Loss of organized atrial contraction predisposes to thromboembolism and stroke.
